audit_items.title: Can the trie._data dictionary contain entries with default values (ghost entries) after trie_set operations?
audit_items.state_context: Prysm BeaconState SSZ Merkleization. Uses dirtyFields map (map[types.FieldIndex]bool), merkleLayers ([][][]byte), stateFieldLeaves (map[types.FieldIndex]*fieldtrie.FieldTrie). Protected by b.lock (sync.RWMutex). No trie._data dictionary concept exists in this codebase.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: PROP-0003 describes ghost entries in a Python EL MPT trie._data dictionary after trie_set deletion operations. The resolved Go code (HashTreeRoot + initializeMerkleLayers) is Prysm's beacon chain SSZ Merkleization — a fundamentally different data structure. There is no trie._data dictionary, no trie_set/trie_delete concept. The nearest analogue is dirtyFields map which tracks fields needing recomputation. initializeMerkleLayers resets dirtyFields to an empty map after full Merkleization, then recomputeDirtyFields processes remaining dirty fields. No ghost entry analogue was found in this code path.
state_anomalies_found: recomputeDirtyFields iterates range b.dirtyFields and deletes entries mid-loop — if rootSelector errors mid-way, subsequent HashTreeRoot call only reprocesses remaining dirty fields (partially consistent state on error path)
No ghost-entry equivalent found in Prysm SSZ Merkle trie
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: merkleLayers acts as a lazy-computed Merkle tree cache. It is lazily initialized by initializeMerkleLayers and cleared (set to nil) on state mutations, forcing recomputation. No stale cache vulnerability found.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: HashTreeRoot acquires b.lock.Lock() (write lock) for the entire operation. initializeMerkleLayers and recomputeDirtyFields both operate under this lock. No concurrent dirty-field corruption possible during HashTreeRoot.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No trie._data, trie_set, or ghost entry concept exists in the target code. The property cannot be tested against this code. The only analogous state-consistency concern (partial dirty-field deletion on error) is a recoverable state that does not corrupt Merkle root output — on next successful HashTreeRoot call, all previously processed fields will have their roots already in merkleLayers[0], and remaining dirty fields will be recomputed.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The EL MPT trie._data ghost entry property is entirely absent from the resolved Prysm beacon chain code. The code mismatch is confirmed — grep_fallback matched on 'trie' keyword in file path/package name rather than semantic function equivalence.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: N/A — property does not map to resolved code

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: INV-006 (no ghost entries in trie._data) cannot be verified against Prysm SSZ Merkleization. The SSZ Merkleization correctly clears dirty fields after recomputation and uses a fixed-size array-based Merkle tree rather than a dictionary. No equivalent of ghost entries is possible in this architecture.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: dirtyFields map is cleared by initializeMerkleLayers (full reset) and delete(b.dirtyFields, field) in recomputeDirtyFields. Fixed-size merkleLayers array prevents ghost entries by design.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for the Prysm SSZ context. The property as stated is inapplicable to this codebase.
edge_cases: recomputeDirtyFields partial failure leaves inconsistent dirty state between calls — recoverable but suboptimal

audit_items.title: Does trie_get correctly return the value set by trie_set, and return trie.default for unset keys?
audit_items.state_context: Prysm BeaconState SSZ Merkleization. No trie_get/trie_set concept exists in Prysm beacon chain.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: PROP-0004 describes the round-trip correctness invariant of Python EL MPT trie_get/trie_set. The resolved Prysm Go code contains neither function. Prysm's beacon state is a struct with typed fields accessed via getter methods (e.g., b.Validators(), b.Balances()), not a key-value trie. Field mutations mark fields dirty, triggering recomputation on next HashTreeRoot call. The invariant that 'read what you wrote' is enforced by Go's type system and the struct field accessors, not by a trie API.
state_anomalies_found: No trie_get/trie_set equivalent found — state is accessed via typed struct getters/setters
No round-trip consistency issue found in the resolved SSZ Merkleization code
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: Prysm uses lazy merkleLayers cache invalidated on mutation. No read-after-write inconsistency in the cache.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Read operations use b.lock.RLock(), write operations use b.lock.Lock(). Read-write ordering is enforced by the mutex.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No trie_get or trie_set function exists in the resolved code. Cannot construct a counterexample for a property about these non-existent functions. The round-trip invariant for Prysm's typed field accessors is guaranteed by Go's type system.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The EL MPT trie_get/trie_set round-trip property has no mapping in the resolved Prysm beacon chain code. Component mismatch confirmed.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: INV-008 (trie_get returns exactly what trie_set stored) is inapplicable to Prysm beacon state, which uses typed struct fields rather than a key-value MPT. The property cannot be proved or disproved against this code.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Go typed struct field accessors enforce read-what-you-wrote invariant at language level
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for the Prysm context; property is inapplicable

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Confirmed component mismatch: PROP-0004 describes Python EL MPT trie_get/trie_set. No such functions exist in Prysm beacon chain Go code. grep_fallback resolution is incorrect.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-resolve against Python ethereum/execution-specs trie module.

audit_items.state_context: Prysm BeaconState SSZ Merkleization. No 'secured trie', keccak256 key hashing, or _prepare_trie concept exists in this beacon chain context.

The 'secured trie' concept (where raw address keys are keccak256-hashed to prevent trie-balancing attacks) is an EL execution layer concern absent from the beacon chain.

audit_items.title: Can encode_node produce empty bytes (b'') for any valid input, violating the non-empty encoding invariant?
audit_items.state_context: Prysm BeaconState SSZ Merkleization. No encode_node function exists in this codebase.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: PROP-0006 describes the Python EL MPT encode_node() function potentially returning empty bytes b'', which would corrupt the MPT structure. The resolved Prysm code has no encode_node function. The nearest Prysm analogue is fieldtrie leaf encoding or rootSelector output, but these always return [32]byte (SHA-256 hash) — never empty. SHA-256 output is always 32 bytes and non-zero for any non-trivial input. The SSZ Merkleization of zero-length leaf would produce SHA-256([]) = e3b0c... (non-empty). No empty encoding scenario possible in Prysm SSZ.
state_anomalies_found: No encode_node function exists in resolved code
SSZ field hashes are always 32 bytes — empty encoding is structurally impossible

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No encode_node function exists in the resolved code. Cannot construct counterexample for a non-existent function. Prysm's SSZ field encodings always produce 32-byte hashes via SHA-256; empty output is impossible by SHA-256 output properties.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: EL MPT encode_node empty-bytes property has no mapping in resolved Prysm code. Component mismatch confirmed.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: INV-017 (encode_node non-empty bytes) is inapplicable. Prysm SSZ uses 32-byte SHA-256 hashes which are structurally non-empty. The invariant holds trivially for SSZ but the property is about a different system.

phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for SSZ context; property is inapplicable

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does encode_node for Account values always receive and use a valid (non-None) storage root from get_storage_root callback?
audit_items.state_context: Prysm BeaconState SSZ Merkleization. No encode_node or get_storage_root callback concept exists. Closest analogue: rootSelector calls latestExecutionPayloadHeader*.HashTreeRoot() — nil dereference possible if header is nil. Constructors prevent nil assignment in normal flows.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: PROP-0007 describes encode_node() for Account values invoking a get_storage_root callback that must return a valid (non-None) EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT for empty storage. The resolved Prysm code has neither concept. The nearest analogue is rootSelector in state_trie.go calling .HashTreeRoot() on latestExecutionPayloadHeader* fields — which could panic if the header pointer is nil. In practice, InitializeFromProto* constructors assign st.LatestExecutionPayloadHeader which is a protobuf message (never nil if decoded from valid proto) and Copy() propagates these correctly.
state_anomalies_found: rootSelector calls b.latestExecutionPayloadHeaderDeneb.HashTreeRoot() without explicit nil check — if Deneb+ state constructed with nil header (deserialization bug), panic would occur
No encode_node or get_storage_root callback exists in resolved code
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: Execution payload headers are direct state fields, not cached values. No staleness concern.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: HashTreeRoot holds full write lock during execution. No concurrent nil-write possible.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The encode_node/get_storage_root callback property has no mapping. The closest nil-dereference scenario for execution payload header requires: (1) Deneb+ state version, (2) nil latestExecutionPayloadHeaderDeneb, (3) rootSelector reached with that field dirty. Constructors prevent condition (2) in normal operation. No external attacker path to force nil header assignment found.
attack_scenarios: If deserialization code incorrectly constructs a Deneb+ BeaconState with nil latestExecutionPayloadHeaderDeneb, rootSelector would panic — but this is an internal invariant violation, not an external attacker scenario

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Trust boundary tb-002 (non-None storage root in encode_node) is an EL MPT concern with no mapping in Prysm beacon chain. The nil-header scenario in rootSelector is an internal defensive concern, not an externally reachable vulnerability.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: N/A — property does not map to resolved code

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: INV-003 (non-None storage root in encode_node callback) is inapplicable to Prysm SSZ. The nil-header concern in rootSelector is mitigated by constructors assigning non-nil headers. An explicit nil check in rootSelector would provide defense-in-depth but is not a security vulnerability in the current code given constructor guarantees.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Constructors (InitializeFromProtoUnsafe*) assign st.LatestExecutionPayloadHeader; version type-switch in rootSelector routes to correct header type; Copy() propagates non-nil headers
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for standard operational paths. Defensive nil check in rootSelector would harden against deserialization edge cases.
edge_cases: Deneb+ state with nil latestExecutionPayloadHeaderDeneb would panic in rootSelector — informational hardening recommendation only
